questions.q: What city was near the place where the people of Israel camped in the plains of Moab on the other side of Jordan River?
questions.a: The city of Jericho was on the other side of the Jordan River near the place where they camped.

questions.q: Why were the people of Moab afraid of the people of Israel?
questions.a: The people of Moab were afraid of the people of Israel because they had seen all that they had done to the Amorites, and because there were many people.

questions.q: Of what country was Balak king?
questions.a: Balak was the king of Moab.

questions.q: What did Balak want Balaam to do to the nation that came from Egypt?
questions.a: Balak wanted Balaam to curse the nation that came from Egypt.

questions.q: Why did Balak want Balaam to curse the nation that had come from Egypt?
questions.a: He wanted Balaam to curse that nation because they covered the face of the earth, they were next to him, and they were too strong for him.

questions.q: What did Balak know that Balaam could do?
questions.a: Balak knew that whomever Balaam blessed would be blessed, and whomever he cursed would be cursed.

questions.q: What Balaam say when he heard Balak’s message?
questions.a: Balaam said that the messengers should stay there overnight and he would bring to them what Yahweh said to him.

questions.q: What did Balaam tell Yahweh about the request of those men who came to him from Balak?
questions.a: Balaam told God that Balak asked him to curse the people of Israel so Balak could fight them and drive them out.

questions.q: What did God tell Balaam to do about going with the messengers and about cursing the people of Israel?
questions.a: God told Balaam that he was not to go with the men and that he was not to curse the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Balaam tell Balak’s leaders in the morning?
questions.a: Balaam told Balak’s leaders to go back to their land because Yahweh refused to allow him to go with them.

questions.q: What did the leaders tell Balak when they went back to him?
questions.a: The leaders told Balak that Balaam refused to come with them.

questions.q: How did Balak try to get Balaam to come to him when he sent more honorable leaders to Balaam?
questions.a: Balak tried to get Balaam to curse Israel by paying him extremely well, giving him great honor, and doing whatever he told him to do.

questions.q: What did Balaam say to Balak’s men in reply to their request?
questions.a: Balaam told them that he could not go beyond the word of Yahweh, his God, and could do neither less nor more than what he old me.

questions.q: Why did Balaam tell Balak’s men they should wait overnight?
questions.a: Balaam told Balak’s men to wait there that night so that he might learn anything further that Yahweh said to him.

questions.q: What did God tell Balaam to do when he came to Balaam at night?
questions.a: When God came to Balaam that night, he told Balaam to get up and go with Balak’s men but to do only what God told him to do.

questions.q: What did Balaam do in the morning?
questions.a: Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the leaders of Moab in the morning.

questions.q: Why was God angry?
questions.a: God was angry because Balaam went with them.

questions.q: What did the angel of Yahweh do?
questions.a: The angel of Yahweh placed himself in the road as an adversary to Balaam.

questions.q: What did Balaam’s donkey see standing in the road?
questions.a: Balaam’s donkey saw the angel of Yahweh standing in the road with his drawn sword in his hand.

questions.q: What did Balaam’s donkey do when he saw the angel of Yahweh, and what did Balaam do to his donkey?
questions.a: Balaam’s donkey turned off the road and went into a field; Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back to the road.

questions.q: What was on the right and left of the angel of Yahweh when he stood in a narrow part of the road between some vineyards?
questions.a: A wall was on the angel’s right side and another wall was on his left side.

questions.q: What did the donkey do when he saw the angel of Yahweh with the drawn sword in the narrow place of the road, and then how did Balaam respond to what his donkey did?
questions.a: When the donkey saw the angel of Yahweh, she struck the wall and pinned Balaam’s foot against it; then Balaam struck her again.

questions.q: What did the donkey do when she saw the angel of Yahweh in another narrow place where there was no way to turn to either side, and what did Balaam do?
questions.a: The donkey laid down under Balaam; Balaam struck the donkey with his staff.

questions.q: What did the donkey ask Balaam when Yahweh opened her mouth so she could talk?
questions.a: The donkey asked Balaam what she had done to him that made him strike her three times.

questions.q: How did Balaam reply to the donkey, and what did he wish he could do to her?
questions.a: Balaam replied to the donkey that he had struck her because she acted so stupidly, and he wished that he had a sword in his hand so that he could kill her.

questions.q: What did Balaam see and do when Yahweh opened his eyes?
questions.a: Balaam saw the angel of Yahweh standing in the road with his drawn sword in his hand so Balaam lowered his head and lay face down.

questions.q: Why did the angel of Yahweh tell Balaam about why his donkey acted the way she did?
questions.a: The angel told Balaam that when his donkey saw the angel she turned away three times.

questions.q: What did the angel say would have happened to Balaam if his donkey had not turned away?
questions.a: The angel told Balaam that if his donkey had not turned away the angel would have killed Balaam and spared the donkey’s life.

questions.q: What did Balaam confess to the angel, and what did he offer to do?
questions.a: Balaam confessed that he had sinned and offered to return to the place from which he had come.

questions.q: How did the angel reply to Balaam?
questions.a: The angel replied that Balaam should go ahead with the men but only speak the words that the angel told him to speak.

questions.q: What did Balak do when he heard that Balaam had come?
questions.a: Balak went out to meet Balaam.

questions.q: What did Balak ask Balaam when he met him at the city of Aron, a city on Moab’s border?
questions.a: Balak asked Balaam why he had not come when Balak summoned him, and did Balaam not think Balak was able to honor him.

questions.q: What did Balaam tell Balak that he could only say?
questions.a: Balaam told Balak that he could only say the words that God put into his mouth.

questions.q: What did Balak do when he and Balaam arrived at Kiriath Huzoth?
questions.a: When they arrived at Kiriath Huzoth, Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep and gave some meat to Balaam and the leaders who were with him.

questions.q: What could Balaam see when Balak took him up to the Bamoth Baal?
questions.a: Balaam could see only the end of the Israelites in their camp.

commentary.text: Balak's fear of Israel, He sends for Balaam.
The opposition to Balaam by the way.

Verses 1–14 The king of Moab formed a plan to get the people of Israel cursed; that is, to set God against them, who had hitherto fought for them. He had a false notion, that if he could get some prophet to pray for evil upon them, and to pronounce a blessing upon himself and his forces, that then he should be able to deal with them. None had so great a reputation as Balaam; and Balak will employ him, though he send a great way for him. It is not known whether the Lord had ever spoken to Balaam, or by him, before this; though it is probable he had, and it is certain he did afterwards. Yet we have abundant proof that he lived and died a wicked man, an enemy to God and his people. And the curse shall not come upon us if there is not a cause, even though men utter it. To prevail with Balaam, they took the wages of unrighteousness, but God laid restraint upon Balaam, forbidding him to curse Israel. Balaam was no stranger to Israel's cause; so that he ought to have answered the messengers at once, that he would never curse a people whom God had blessed; but he takes a night's time to consider what he should do. When we parley with temptations, we are in great danger of being overcome. Balaam was not faithful in returning God's answer to the messengers. Those are a fair mark for Satan's temptation, who lessen Divine restraints; as if to go against God's law were only to go without his leave. The messengers also are not faithful in returning Balaam's answer to Balak. Thus many are abused by the flatteries of those about them, and are prevented from seeing their own faults and follies.

A second embassy was sent to Balaam. It were well for us, if we were as earnest and constant in prosecuting a good work, notwithstanding disappointments. Balak laid a bait, not only for Balaam's covetousness, but for his pride and ambition. How earnestly should we beg of God daily to mortify such desires in us! Thus sinners stick at no pains, spare no cost, and care not how low they stoop, to gratify their luxury, or their malice. Shall we then be unwilling to do what is right? God forbid! Balaam's convictions charged him to keep to the command of God; nor could any man have spoken better. But many call God theirs, who are not his, not truly because not only his. There is no judging men by their words; God knows the heart. Balaam's corruptions at the same time inclined him to go contrary to the command. He seemed to refuse the temptation; but he expressed no abhorrence of it. He had a strong desire to accept the offer, and hoped that God might give him leave to go. He had already been told what the will of God was. It is a certain evidence of the ruling of corruption in the heart, to beg leave to sin. God gave Balaam up to his own heart's lusts. As God sometimes denies the prayers of his people in love, so sometimes he grants the desires of the wicked in wrath.

We must not think, that because God does not always by his providence restrain men from sin, therefore he approves of it, or that it is not hateful to him. The holy angels oppose sin, and perhaps are employed in preventing it more than we are aware. This angel was an adversary to Balaam, because Balaam counted him his adversary; those are really our best friends, and we ought so to reckon them, who stop our progress in sinful ways. Balaam has notice of God's displeasure by the ass. It is common for those whose hearts are fully set in them to do evil, to push on violently, through the difficulties Providence lays in their way. The Lord opened the mouth of the ass. This was a great miracle wrought by the power of God. He who made man speak, could, when he pleased, make the ass to speak with man's voice. The ass complained of Balaam's cruelty. The righteous God does not allow the meanest or weakest to be abused; but they shall be able to speak in their own defence, or he will some way or other speak for them. Balaam at length has his eyes opened. God has many ways to bring down the hard and unhumbled heart. When our eyes are opened, we shall see the danger of sinful ways, and how much it was for our advantage to be crossed. Balaam seemed to relent; I have sinned; but it does not appear that he was sensible of this wickedness of his heart, or willing to own it. If he finds he cannot go forward, he will be content, since there is no remedy, to go back. Thus many leave their sins, only because their sins have left them. The angel declared that he should not only be unable to curse Israel, but should be forced to bless them: this would be more for the glory of God, and to his own confusion, than if he had turned back.

Balak has now nothing to complain of, but that Balaam did not come sooner. Balaam bids Balak not depend too much upon him. He seems to speak with vexation; but is really as desirous to please Balak, as ever he had pretended to be to please God. See what need we have to pray every day, Our Father which art in heaven, lead us not into temptation. Let us be jealous over our own hearts, seeing how far men may go in the knowledge of God, and yet come short of Divine grace.
